finalReport:
# OpenCode × OpenCut Integration — Technical Feasibility Today

## Objective and verdict

**Question:** Can a stable OpenCode integration be built around OpenCut today?

**Answer: No — not stable.** A demo-grade integration is feasible today as a locally-pinned, browser-in-the-loop workaround. A stable, headless, versioned integration is blocked pending first-party Editor API / MCP / headless / portable project format from the rewrite.

This distinction is the core of the report. Every section below labels claims as **Verified fact**, **Roadmap**, **Workaround**, **Inference**, or **Uncertainty**.

**Budget disclosure:** Research hit completion reserve with 2/6 questions sufficient (editor/timeline, persistence). Export/rendering limits, full automation/process-boundary detail, desktop distribution/back-compat, and licensing were not fully verified to criterion. One claim is PARTIAL-critical (export limits), one non-critical PARTIAL (desktop), one UNSUPPORTED (license file). See Remaining uncertainties.

---

## 1. Editor state — Verified fact: usable today is classic, main is rewrite

**Verified fact:** The main OpenCut repo declares it “is being rewritten from the ground up” with coming items: Editor API, plugin-first architecture, Rust core for desktop/mobile/browser, MCP server for AI agents, headless mode, and in-editor scripting tab. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

**Verified fact:** The same README directs users to the previous version as “the one to reach for today,” noting the hosted app still runs classic and the rewrite lives separately until ready to take over. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

**Implication (Inference):** Any OpenCode work today must target archived classic, not main. Pin to a specific classic commit; do not track main. Main has explicitly paused outside contributions while architecture is designed.

## 2. Timeline manipulation — Verified fact: UI-driven; no first-party programmatic path

**Verified fact:** Classic uses an `EditorCore` singleton with specialized managers — TimelineManager, ScenesManager, ProjectManager, MediaManager, RendererManager, Save/Audio/Selection managers — plus Zustand stores, exposing multi-track timeline (video/audio/overlay tracks) and real-time preview. [Architecture](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture)

**Verified fact — Workaround only:** There is no stable first-party timeline API. Community MCP bridges get control only by patching the web app to expose `window.__opencut` (EditorCore) and `window.__stores` and driving them via Playwright `page.evaluate()`. [MCP bridge design](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)

**Verified fact:** That workaround explicitly requires the Legacy Next.js App Router build with complete editor/timeline/stores; the current public rewrite is incomplete and production hosted builds do not expose internal hooks — local run required. [Controller requirements](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)

**Labels:**
- UI trim/split/move/duplicate/text/audio/effects/keyframes/history: **Verified fact** as UI capabilities via manager/store model.
- Programmatic timeline edits from OpenCode without a browser: **Not available — Roadmap**.
- Programmatic edits via patched local Chromium: **Workaround — verified to exist, not stable**.

## 3. Persistence — Verified fact: browser-local, no portable contract

**Verified fact:** Classic `StorageService` persists projects and media metadata in IndexedDB (`video-editor-projects`, `video-editor-media`) and media bytes in OPFS (`media-files`), later refactored to per-project DBs plus per-project timeline store, with blob object URLs at runtime. [Storage implementation](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/09373eb4a3f792d96d97d81f4fb86539d76e5702)

**Verified fact:** Docs confirm: browser storage (IndexedDB for project data/metadata, OPFS for media, localStorage for prefs), nothing sent to servers, offline-capable. [Project management docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/features/project-management)

**Verified fact — Blocking:** There is no portable versioned project file. Projects are locked in IndexedDB/OPFS, cannot be saved/shared/moved between devices; the feature request explicitly notes external tools have no way to programmatically generate a project and asks for versioned JSON Schema with media by filename. [Portable format request](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)

**Inference:** OpenCode cannot today write a file to disk and expect OpenCut to open it. It must either drive live in-browser state or reverse-engineer internal `SerializedProject`/`TimelineData` — both fragile.

## 4. Media storage — Verified fact + fragility

Covered above, plus:

**Verified fact:** Without OPFS, large media falls back to in-memory storage; Safari File System Access was behind flags. [OPFS Safari notes](https://opencut.dev/faq/opencut-opfs-safari/)

**Verified fact:** Persistence races are reported: rename/delete not ordered with autosave, errors swallowed as success, half-deleted projects possible with no per-project fence. [Persistence race bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/873)

**Labels:**
- Local-first privacy (no server upload): **Verified fact**.
- Cross-browser large-media reliability, concurrent rename/delete safety: **Workaround/Uncertainty — do not build file sync on this**.

## 5. Rendering / export — PARTIAL: in-browser only, limits unverified

**Verified fact (partial):** Rendering is owned by `RendererManager` inside the live editor; community bridges reuse that in-page export path rather than a separate headless renderer. [Architecture](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture) [MCP bridge design](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)

**Uncertainty (budget-blocked):** Exact resolution/FPS/codec/format limits, faster-than-realtime vs realtime behavior, WebCodecs/MediaRecorder/FFmpeg fallbacks, and true headless batch rendering could not be verified to criterion before reserve. Do not assume 1080p/4K, MP4/WebM parity, or background render without further primary-code verification.

**Roadmap:** Headless mode and batch rendering are listed as coming, not present. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

**Inference:** Today export requires an open Chromium page with media already in OPFS/blob URLs. No evidence supports OpenCode triggering render as a pure CLI/subprocess today.

## 6. Automation surface, MCP/API status, process boundary

**Verified fact:** First-party MCP server, Editor API, headless mode, scripting tab are roadmap, not shipped. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

**Verified fact — Workaround:** Community servers expose ~161 tools via Playwright injection into `window.__opencut` / `window.__stores` over stdio, plus fetch to local app APIs. This is unofficial, patched, and version-pinned. [MCP bridge design](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)

**Verified fact — Process boundary:** OpenCode (Node/subprocess) → MCP stdio → Playwright Chromium → `page.evaluate()` → in-browser EditorCore/Zustand → IndexedDB/OPFS → in-browser RendererManager → download blob. No direct REST/CLI/file boundary is stable; production hosted app boundary is closed. [MCP bridge design](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP) [Controller requirements](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)

**Labels:**
- Official CLI/REST/MCP/headless: **Verified absent — Roadmap**.
- Community MCP + `window.__opencutAutomation`-style bridge: **Workaround**.
- Stable cross-process contract: **Uncertainty — none verified**.

## 7. Desktop availability, backward compat / schema stability

**PARTIAL (non-critical):** Single-codebase desktop/mobile via Rust core is a rewrite goal, not a shipped stable distribution in committed evidence. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

**Inference from workaround constraint:** Because automation requires legacy Next.js classic locally, and production hooks are absent, desktop distribution cannot be assumed as an automation target. [Controller requirements](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)

**Verified fact — Instability signal:** Internal storage has already churned (global → per-project DBs) with no versioned compat policy; portable schema is requested but missing; persistence races exist. [Storage implementation](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/09373eb4a3f792d96d97d81f4fb86539d76e5702) [Portable format request](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719) [Persistence race bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/873)

**Uncertainty:** Official versioning, migration, deprecation policy, and desktop installer signing/distribution were not verified before reserve. Third-party installer claims were observed but not committed as evidence — do not rely on them.

## 8. Licensing — UNSUPPORTED (must re-verify)

Search signals consistently suggested MIT, but no LICENSE file evidence was committed before budget reserve. Treat commercial reuse, embedding, forking, and AI-training implications as **Uncertainty**.

**Required blocking evidence before productizing:** fetch and pin the LICENSE file from the exact classic commit you ship, confirm copyright holder, confirm no additional terms in app config/docs, and get legal review for bundled FFmpeg/codec and asset-license (music/sticker) boundaries.

---

## 9. Feasible-today architecture (demo-grade, explicitly fragile)

Use only for prototypes, with pinned commits and human-in-the-loop export.

```
OpenCode agent
  → local MCP stdio server (community, pinned fork)
  → Playwright Chromium (headed for debug, headless for run)
  → locally-run patched classic build (pinned commit, NEXT-style local dev)
       window.__opencut / window.__stores via page.evaluate()
  → IndexedDB (project/timeline) + OPFS (media bytes) + blob URLs
  → in-page RendererManager export → manual download/blob capture
```

**Rules for today:**
1. Pin `opencut-classic` commit + MCP controller commit; vendor patches in your repo.
2. Run editor locally; never target hosted production.
3. Copy media into the browser via the bridge (do not write IndexedDB/OPFS directly).
4. Serialize intent in your own versioned Draft JSON outside OpenCut, then compile to bridge calls — because OpenCut has no stable import schema. [Portable format request](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)
5. Expect breakage on any editor upgrade; gate with smoke tests (create → add media → split/trim → text → export → verify file).
6. Avoid Safari/OPFS edge cases and concurrent rename/delete during automation. [OPFS Safari notes](https://opencut.dev/faq/opencut-opfs-safari/) [Persistence race bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/873)

## 10. Preferred future architecture (stable — pending upstream)

```
OpenCode agent
  → versioned DraftTemplate JSON (zod/JSON Schema, media by content hash + filename)
  → first-party @opencut/render-sdk library + CLI (Node/TS + subprocess for Python/Go)
  → RenderServer (long-lived) → headless Chromium OR Rust wgpu compositor + ffmpeg
  → first-party Editor API / MCP server / scripting tab in editor
  → portable .opencut file ↔ editor preview ↔ byte-identical export
```

This mirrors the direction already proposed upstream as opt-in automation with stable LLM-friendly schema and reuse of the UI export path — but that proposal is not merged first-party and Rust coverage is partial. Do not present it as available.

Wait for: Editor API + versioned JSON Schema + first-party MCP + headless `render draft.json -o out.mp4` + signed desktop + migration policy. All are listed as coming. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)

## 11. Blocking evidence (what would flip the verdict)

1. First-party Editor API / MCP server merged (not community patch). Currently roadmap. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)
2. Headless/CLI render that is byte-identical to UI export without open UI. Currently roadmap/workaround only. [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md) [MCP bridge design](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)
3. Portable versioned project JSON with import/export + schema docs. Currently explicitly missing. [Portable format request](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)
4. Schema stability / migration guarantee + persistence race fix. Currently churning and racy. [Storage implementation](https://github.com/realtgy/OpenCut/commit/09373eb4a3f792d96d97d81f4fb86539d76e5702) [Persistence race bug](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/873)
5. Verified export matrix (resolutions/FPS/codecs/containers, realtime factor, hardware acceleration, failure modes). Currently PARTIAL.
6. Verified desktop distribution + back-compat policy. Currently PARTIAL.
7. Verified LICENSE file + governance for fork/embed. Currently UNSUPPORTED.

## 12. Remaining uncertainties (budget-exhausted)

- Export limits, headless constraints, MediaRecorder/WebCodecs/ffmpeg behavior: PARTIAL — needs `scene-exporter`, `video-export` package, and export dialog primary-code reads.
- Desktop installers, Tauri vs GPUI status, mobile parity: PARTIAL — needs desktop README/releases primary reads.
- License/commercial terms: UNSUPPORTED — needs LICENSE fetch.
- No contradictions recorded; disagreements are roadmap-vs-workaround, not factual conflict.

## Research limitations
- Research budget exhausted (completion_reserve).

- Reportable claim claim-0010 is UNSUPPORTED: OpenCut license and commercial reuse terms (widely signaled as MIT) were not verified against a committed LICENSE file before budget reserve.

Research completed in 1m 34s · 32 citations · 6 searches

Scope: stable OpenCode integration around OpenCut — editor/timeline, persistence/media, export, MCP/API/process boundary, desktop/compat, licensing.

Findings: Usable editor today is archived `opencut-classic` (UI-driven EditorCore+Zustand multi-track); main repo is incomplete rewrite. No first-party Editor API/MCP/headless — roadmap only. Programmatic control today is patched Playwright `window.__opencut` workaround requiring local classic. Persistence is IndexedDB+OPFS browser-local with no portable versioned project file. Export is in-browser via RendererManager — exact limits unverified. Desktop/Rust single-codebase is future goal; storage has churned with persistence races.

Feasible today: demo-grade browser-in-the-loop (OpenCode → community MCP stdio → Playwright → pinned local classic → IndexedDB/OPFS → in-page export). Preferred future: versioned Draft JSON → first-party render SDK/CLI → headless/Rust compositor + MCP/Editor API + portable `.opencut`.

Uncertainty (budget reserve hit, 2/6 questions sufficient): export matrix PARTIAL, desktop distribution PARTIAL, license UNSUPPORTED — must re-verify LICENSE file, export code, desktop releases before productizing.

claimSummaries.statement: The usable OpenCut editor today is opencut-classic; the main OpenCut repo is an incomplete ground-up rewrite and opencut.app still runs classic.
Classic editor is UI-driven multi-track (video/audio/overlay) built on EditorCore singleton managers and Zustand stores with real-time preview.
No stable first-party programmatic timeline API exists today; community MCP control works only as a patched Playwright workaround requiring a locally run classic build.
Projects and media are persisted browser-locally: IndexedDB for project/metadata and OPFS for media bytes (later per-project stores), with blob object URLs at runtime.
There is no portable versioned .opencut JSON project file or stable import path; projects are locked in IndexedDB/OPFS with no programmatic generation contract.
First-party MCP server, Editor API, headless mode and scripting tab are roadmap items, not available today; community 161-tool MCPs are unofficial workarounds.

Export/rendering today is in-browser via RendererManager driven from the live editor page, requiring an open Chromium page; exact resolution/FPS/format limits and true headless batch rendering are not established from committed evidence.
Desktop/mobile from one Rust core is a rewrite goal; no verified stable desktop distribution or backward-compat policy exists in committed evidence — classic desktop was opt-in/in-progress.
OPFS/Safari fallbacks and rename/delete persistence races make direct storage-level integration fragile.
OpenCut license and commercial reuse terms (widely signaled as MIT) were not verified against a committed LICENSE file before budget reserve.
